claims.text: The Pulumi `protect` resource option is a Pulumi-engine construct enforced entirely within Pulumi.
The Pulumi `protect` resource option is never sent to the cloud provider.
A GCP Cloud SQL instance has a `deletionProtection` attribute that is a cloud-provider deletion-protection setting separate from Pulumi's `protect`.
An AWS RDS instance has a `deletionProtection` attribute that is a cloud-provider deletion-protection setting separate from Pulumi's `protect`.
The cloud provider enforces resource-level deletion-protection attributes (such as `deletionProtection`) independently of anything Pulumi knows about.
A resource can be unprotected in Pulumi and still refuse to delete due to cloud-provider deletion protection, or be protected in Pulumi yet the provider-level deletion protection be off (vice versa).

The Pulumi docs page at /docs/iac/operations/troubleshooting/destroy-failures/ has a section 'Deletion protection on the resource itself' explaining how to tell Pulumi protect and provider deletion protection apart and resolve each.
Many cloud resources carry their own deletion-protection attributes that the provider or the cloud API enforces independently of Pulumi's `protect` resource option.
GCP Cloud SQL instances have a `deletionProtection` attribute (deletion-protection property) in the Pulumi provider.
AWS RDS instances have a `deletionProtection` attribute (deletion-protection property) in the Pulumi provider.
Pulumi's `protect` option and resource-level deletion-protection attributes are complementary rather than substitutes for one another.

The Pulumi docs page /docs/iac/operations/troubleshooting/destroy-failures/ has a section 'Deletion protection on the resource itself' explaining how to tell the two layers apart and resolve a destroy failure caused by either.
Pulumi has no single flag to protect every resource in a stack; stack transforms can set `protect: true` on every resource as it is registered.

Three distinct layers can hold deletion protection that causes a `pulumi destroy` failure (Pulumi's `protect` option, a provider-enforced flag, and a cloud-API-enforced protection), and the error message usually indicates which one was hit.
Pulumi's `protect` resource option is an engine-level guard that never reaches the cloud provider.
An error naming a URN and mentioning `protect` indicates the Pulumi `protect` resource option blocked the destroy.
The page /docs/iac/concepts/resources/options/protect/ exists and explains how to remove the `protect` resource option.

Some Pulumi providers refuse to issue the delete call at all when a resource carries a deletion-protection attribute, e.g. `deletionProtection` on `gcp.sql.DatabaseInstance` or `gcp.container.Cluster`.
For provider-enforced deletion protection, the failure surfaces from the provider before any request reaches the cloud API.
`gcp.sql.DatabaseInstance` and `gcp.container.Cluster` have a `deletionProtection` property.
AWS RDS `deletionProtection`, EC2 `disableApiTermination`, and Azure Resource Manager management locks are enforced by the cloud API itself, independent of Pulumi.
Cloud-API-enforced deletion protection errors come back from the cloud provider's API, often with a distinct error code such as `ScopeLocked` (Azure).

`pulumi destroy` deletes what is already recorded in the stack's state, not what the program currently says, so setting the deletion-protection attribute to `false` in the program alone is not enough.

Remediation for provider-enforced and cloud-API-enforced deletion protection is: set the attribute to `false` in the program, run `pulumi up` so the change reaches the live resource and Pulumi's state, then run `pulumi destroy`.

If deletion protection was already disabled outside Pulumi (e.g. in the cloud console), `pulumi refresh` synchronizes the stack state with reality and `pulumi destroy` then succeeds without an intervening `pulumi up`.
`gcp.sql.DatabaseInstance`'s `deletionProtection` is provider-enforced, and a nested `settings.deletionProtectionEnabled` also guards the instance at the GCP API level.
`gcp.container.Cluster`'s `deletionProtection` is provider-enforced.
`gcp.bigquery.Table` has a provider-enforced `deletionProtection` attribute.
Destroying a `gcp.bigquery.Dataset` that still contains tables fails unless `deleteContentsOnDestroy` is `true`.
`aws.rds.Instance` and `aws.rds.Cluster` `deletionProtection` is enforced by the AWS API and defaults to `false`.
`aws.s3.BucketV2` `forceDestroy` defaults to `false`, and a non-empty bucket otherwise fails to delete.
`aws.ec2.Instance` `disableApiTermination` is enforced by the AWS API (EC2 termination protection).
`aws.dynamodb.Table` `deletionProtectionEnabled` is enforced by the AWS API and defaults to `false`.
`azure-native.authorization.ManagementLockByScope` and scope-specific variants such as `ManagementLockAtResourceLevel` exist as resources for Azure management locks.
Azure management locks are enforced by Azure Resource Manager; a `CanNotDelete` lock must be removed before the resource can be deleted, independent of the Pulumi program.
Destroying an `azure-native.keyvault.Vault` only soft-deletes it; recreating a vault with the same name fails with `VaultAlreadyExists` until the soft-deleted vault is purged or recovered.
Azure Key Vault purge protection prevents purging a soft-deleted vault until its retention period elapses.
